claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
Pack cementation at approximately 1000 °C for several hours can deposit a controlled silicide layer on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The resulting silicide layer will be approximately 10–50 µm thick.
The treatment will produce a continuous, adherent silicide surface scale.
A silicide surface layer can improve oxidation resistance.
The continuous silicide scale will act as a diffusion barrier that reduces oxygen ingress into the alloy bulk.
Reduced oxygen ingress will mitigate or prevent pesting of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Confining the treatment to the surface will leave the bulk microstructure essentially unchanged.
The surface treatment will not materially degrade room-temperature or 1000 °C tensile properties.
Treated specimens will have lower mass gain and less scale spallation than untreated specimens during exposure to air.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes oxidation-induced pesting during air exposure for at least 5 hours at high temperature.
The proposed protection is expected to apply in air from 800 to 1000 °C for exposures of 5 hours or longer.
Restricting the silicide layer to approximately 10–50 µm will avoid adverse near-surface embrittlement during mechanical loading.
The effects of the treatment on long-term adhesion, cyclic loading, fatigue, and fracture behavior remain undetermined.
A controlled comparison will use treated and untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr specimens exposed to air at 900 °C for 5 hours.
The hypothesis is falsified if treatment provides no distinguishable oxidation benefit or significantly degrades tensile ductility or yield strength.
